_comment: Fill in a family label for each role name, then pass this file with --role-map. Publish it alongside your results.

Endgame Conversion Specialist: Assesses whether trades and simplifications favor White's winning chances, and evaluates pawn races, king activity, and technical winning methods. Advises when to trade pieces versus keep tension

Assesses whether trades and simplifications favor White's winning chances, evaluating pawn races, king activity, and technical winning plans. Advises when to trade pieces versus keep complexity to exploit Stockfish's weaknesses
Assesses which trades and simplifications favor White's winning chances, evaluates pawn promotion races and king activity, and steers the game toward technically winning endgames
Assesses which trades and simplifications favor the team, evaluating pawn races, piece-versus-pawn imbalances, and winning technique. Judges whether a proposed line leads to a convertible advantage

Evaluates whether candidate moves preserve or improve winning chances in simplified positions, including trades, pawn races, and king activity. Advises on which exchanges convert an advantage and which waste it
Evaluates which simplifications and trades favor White's winning chances, and checks whether candidate moves lead to won or drawn endgame types
Evaluates which simplifications and trades favor White's winning chances, and judges whether a given structure or material balance can be converted. Advises on pawn promotion races and piece trades

Evaluates which trades and simplifications convert advantages into wins, using known endgame technique and piece-count reasoning. Advises when to trade pieces or push passed pawns to lock in a winning position
Evaluates which trades and simplifications favor the team, assesses pawn races, king activity, and winning technique, and advises whether to keep or exchange material
Endgame Converter: Assesses which trades and simplifications favor the team, evaluates pawn races and king activity, and steers the game toward technically winning endgames when material or structure favors White

Evaluates how each candidate move affects simplification and the likely endgame, favoring trades and structures that convert material advantages into wins. Judges whether a position is technically winning even if it is currently equal
Evaluates simplification choices and winning technique, judging whether trades and pawn races favor the team and how to convert advantages into a won position
Endgame Planner: Assesses how candidate moves affect future simplifications, pawn races, and conversion of advantages, favoring trades and structures that lead to winning endgames

Evaluates how candidate moves affect the transition into endgame, including piece trades, king activity, passed pawns, and conversion technique. Advises whether simplifying or keeping pieces better serves White's winning chances
Evaluates which simplifications and pawn or piece trades lead to winning or drawn endgames, and steers the game toward favorable technical conditions when the middlegame is balanced
Endgame Technician: Assesses how each candidate move affects simplification, piece trades, and winning technique in the likely endgame, including pawn promotion races and known winning patterns. Recommends trades that convert advantages and avoids trades that reduce winning chances
Assesses how the position will transform into an endgame, judging piece trades, passed pawns, king activity, and conversion technique, and flags moves that trade toward drawn or winning endings

Assesses how trades, piece simplification, and king activity affect winning chances, focusing on converting advantages and holding drawn or worse positions. Advises whether to trade pieces or keep tension

Assesses the simplification and conversion potential of each candidate, recognizing known winning techniques, opposition, and drawing fortresses. Advises on whether to trade pieces or keep tension to reach a convertible endgame
Evaluates how candidate moves affect the likely simplified endgame, including pawn races, piece trades, and conversion techniques. Helps the team steer toward winning or drawing-resistant endgames

Evaluates how candidate moves affect the likely transition to an endgame, including material simplification, pawn races, king activity, and known winning or drawing technique. Prefers moves that convert advantages cleanly

Evaluates how each candidate affects the transition to the endgame, including material balance, pawn promotion paths, king activity, and known theoretical wins or draws. Advises on simplification versus maintaining complexity
Evaluates simplification choices and converts advantages through known endgame techniques, pawn promotion races, and king activity. Advises on whether trades favor the team's winning chances
Evaluates trade decisions and piece exchanges through the lens of the resulting endgame, judging whether simplification favors White's winning chances and which conversion technique applies
Evaluates trades, pawn promotion races, and conversion techniques, judging whether simplifying lines favor the team. Advises when to trade pieces or keep tension to convert an advantage

Evaluates trades, pawn races, and simplification choices by assessing whether the resulting endgame is winning, drawn, or lost. Advises on converting material advantages and on avoiding drawn or lost simplified positions

Evaluates whether candidate moves lead to simplified positions that are winnable, recognizing known theoretical wins, drawn fortresses, and conversion techniques. Advises on trading pieces when advantageous
Evaluates whether trades and simplifications favor White's winning chances, applying known endgame principles, conversion techniques, and piece-value imbalances
Material And Risk Auditor: Acts as a devil's advocate: identifies the worst-case Stockfish reply for each candidate move, scores downside risk, and flags moves that trade material or weaken the king unnecessarily

Acts as a skeptic: checks every candidate for opponent replies that win material, create unstoppable threats, or expose the king. Assigns a risk rating and flags moves whose downside outweighs their upside
Material And Safety Auditor: Acts as a skeptic: checks every candidate for hanging pieces, undefended pieces, back-rank weaknesses, and opponent replies that win material. Vetoes moves that create unacceptable risk
Acts as a skeptic: checks every proposed move for blunders, hanging pieces, unprotected pieces, pins, forks, and opponent replies that win material. Vetoes moves that fail this check

Adversarially checks every candidate move for blunders: hanging pieces, undefended pawns, illegal or unsafe king exposure, and Stockfish's best replies. Acts as a red-team reviewer who tries to refute proposals
Material Safety Auditor: Acts as a risk checker focused on what can go wrong: hanging pieces, overloaded defenders, back-rank weaknesses, and Stockfish's best replies to each candidate. Vetoes moves that lose material or allow a decisive counter
Acts as a risk checker: verifies that each candidate move does not hang pieces, allow forks, pins, or discovered attacks, and quantifies the worst-case material loss
Acts as a skeptic by checking every candidate move for blunders: hanging pieces, undefended squares, illegal moves, and opponent replies that win material. Vetoes moves that fail this check

Acts as a skeptic who checks every candidate for blunders: undefended pieces, pins, discovered attacks, back-rank issues, and Stockfish's strongest replies. Vetoes any move that loses material without compensation
Acts as a skeptic who checks every candidate for hanging pieces, undefended pieces, pins, skewers, and overlooked Black counterplay. Vetoes moves that lose material without compensation

Acts as a skeptic who checks every candidate move for blunders: hanging pieces, undefended squares, illegal or unsafe king exposure, and Stockfish's strongest replies. Vetoes moves that lose material without compensation
Acts as a skeptic who checks every candidate move for blunders: pieces left undefended, squares newly exposed to attack, and opponent replies that win material. Vetoes moves that fail a safety check

Acts as a skeptic who checks every candidate move for hanging pieces, undefended pieces, illegal or unsafe moves, and opponent replies that win material. Vetoes moves that lose material without compensation

Acts as a skeptic who checks every proposed move for blunders: undefended pieces, back-rank weaknesses, discovered attacks, and Stockfish's strongest replies. Vetoes moves that carry unacceptable risk
Acts as a skeptic who checks every proposed move for hanging pieces, undefended pieces, pins, skewers, and Stockfish's most likely reply. Vetoes moves that lose material without compensation
Acts as a skeptic who stress-tests every candidate move for blunders, hanging pieces, overlooked Black captures, and checks. Its sole job is to reject moves that lose material or allow mating nets
Acts as a skeptic: challenges every proposed move by checking for hanging pieces, unprotected pieces, and Stockfish's best recaptures, and vetoes moves that lose material without compensation

Acts as a skeptical checker that identifies every piece left undefended, every square exposed to attack, and every move that allows Stockfish a strong reply or sacrifice. Vetoes candidates with unacceptable risk

Checks every candidate move for hanging pieces, undefended pawns, and simple one-move blunders, including Stockfish's replies such as checks, forks, pins, and discovered attacks. Acts as a veto on moves that lose material without compensation
Materialist Safety Auditor: Acts as a devil's advocate by assuming Stockfish plays the strongest reply, checking every candidate for blunders, hanging pieces, and unsound sacrifices, and rejecting moves whose downside is severe
Acts as a skeptical devil's advocate: attacks every proposed move by searching for Black's best reply, sacrifices, and hidden material losses, and rates the risk of each candidate
Opening And Structure Analyst: Tracks the game's opening or middlegame phase, identifies known theory and Stockfish's likely responses, and flags moves that deviate into unclear or poorly understood positions. Suggests principled development and center control
Opening And Structure Historian: Identifies the current opening or middlegame pattern and recalls established theory and typical plans for both sides. Warns when the team is drifting into known bad structures or deviating from sound main lines
Identifies the opening line on the board, recalls known sound plans and common traps for both sides, and flags when Stockfish's reply is a known book or theoretical move
Identifies the opening or middlegame pattern on the board, recalls established theory and typical plans, and flags when a move departs from known sound continuations
Identifies the opening or middlegame pattern on the board, recalls established theory and typical plans, and warns when a move deviates from well-known principles or leads to known traps

Identifies the opening system and its known main lines, comparing candidate moves against established theory and typical plans for both sides. Warns when the team leaves known theory into unclear territory

Identifies the opening system and its known theory, recognizes familiar middlegame pawn structures, and warns when the position departs from principled play. Suggests moves consistent with established plans
Identifies the opening system and its known theory, recognizes which Stockfish responses are likely, and recommends development moves that follow sound principles and established plans
Identifies the opening system and known theory, recalls standard plans and typical pawn structures, and flags when the position leaves known theory so the team can rely on principled development
Identifies the opening system and known theory, recognizes Stockfish's likely setup, and advises on development order and pawn breaks suited to the current position

Identifies the opening system and known theory, recognizes Stockfish's likely setups, and flags when a move departs from sound principles of development, center control, and king safety. Compares the position to established model structures
Identifies the opening system, known theory, and typical plans and pitfalls for the current position. Warns when a move departs from sound principles of development and center control
Identifies the opening system, known theory, and typical plans from the move sequence so far. Warns when the team leaves book lines or when Stockfish is likely to play a known response
Identifies the opening system, recognizes known theory and common traps for both sides, and judges whether a move follows sound development principles
Recalls established opening theory, known pawn-structure plans, and common middlegame patterns relevant to the current position, and flags when a move departs from well-tested continuations
Recognizes the opening being played, known theory and typical plans for both sides, and the pawn-structure consequences of moves. Warns when a move leaves known theory into unclear territory

Tracks the game's opening theory, known engine-resistant lines, and pawn-structure types from master games. Suggests moves that steer toward positions where White's known plans are reliable against engine play

Tracks the game's opening theory, known sound plans, and typical pawn-structure outcomes, flagging when the position leaves book and what established ideas apply. Advises on development order and known traps
Opening And Structure Scholar: Recognizes known opening theory, standard pawn structures, and typical plans for the current position, and checks whether candidate moves follow sound principles of development and coordination
Opening And Structure Specialist: Assesses moves against established opening theory and common pawn-structure themes, recognizing known plans and well-studied continuations. Warns when the position departs from principled development
Assesses opening principles, development, center control, and known theory relevant to the current position. Flags early structural weaknesses that could cost the game later

Recognizes the opening and early middlegame setup, applies established theory and principles (development, center control, king safety), and suggests moves that keep the team's position sound during the early phase
Opening And Structure Theorist: Assesses the current move in terms of opening principles, development, and pawn-structure consequences, drawing on known theory and typical plans. Flags moves that deviate from sound development
Opening Theorist: Identifies known opening theory and sound development patterns for the current position, recommending moves that follow principles such as central control, rapid development, and castling
Identifies the opening or middlegame theory, known lines, and standard plans relevant to the current position, and flags when a move departs from sound book play
Recalls established opening theory and principles (development, center control, king safety) for the early moves, and flags when the position leaves known book lines and calculation must take over
Recognizes known opening and early middlegame theory, identifies Stockfish's likely responses based on its typical play, and proposes established setups for White
Recognizes known opening and early middlegame theory, suggesting principled development moves and identifying when Stockfish's replies deviate from main lines
Opponent Modeler: Assesses Stockfish's tendencies, such as its strength at deep tactics and its evaluation horizon, and identifies lines that are objectively sound but complex enough to create practical chances. Suggests moves that maximize winning chances against this specific opponent

Models Stockfish's likely replies and tendencies, identifying lines where the engine's best response is hard to find or where it may be steered into imbalanced positions. Flags moves that are objectively sound but practically tricky

Models Stockfish's likely replies and tendencies, identifying which candidate moves lead to positions where the engine's best replies are hardest to find or where its evaluation horizon may be exploited. Challenges the team to consider the engine's best responses rather than assumed replies

Models Stockfish's likely replies and the engine's style and evaluation tendencies, identifying which of our candidate moves lead to positions where the engine's best reply is hardest to find or where its evaluation horizon misjudges the danger
Positional Strategist: Evaluates long-term factors such as pawn structure, piece activity, king safety, and control of key squares. Proposes plans that improve White's position even when no immediate tactic exists
Evaluates long-term factors such as piece activity, king safety, pawn structure, and control of key squares. Proposes plans that build advantages over many moves rather than immediate gains
Evaluates long-term factors such as piece activity, king safety, pawn structure, and control of key squares. Proposes plans that improve White's position even when no immediate tactic exists
Evaluates long-term factors such as piece activity, king safety, pawn structure, center control, and space. Proposes plans that build advantage over many moves

Evaluates long-term factors such as piece activity, king safety, pawn structure, control of central squares, and weak squares. Proposes plans that improve the team's position even when no immediate tactic exists
Evaluates long-term factors such as piece activity, king safety, pawn structure, control of squares, and space. Proposes plans that improve White's position even when no immediate tactic exists

Evaluates long-term structure: pawn formation, king safety, piece activity, control of key squares, and endgame prospects. Proposes plans that improve the position even when no immediate tactic exists
Evaluates pawn structure, piece activity, king safety, and control of key squares to identify the strategic plan that best improves White's position
Evaluates pawn structure, piece activity, king safety, and control of key squares to propose moves that improve the team's long-term position. Argues for plans rather than immediate material gains

Risk And Safety Auditor: Acts as a devil's advocate by scanning every candidate for opponent replies that create threats, hanging pieces, or perpetual-check resources. Assigns a risk rating to each candidate move

Adversarially attacks every proposed move by searching for Stockfish's best refutation, including sacrifices and tactical shots, and estimates the evaluation swing. Vetoes moves whose downside is severe
Risk Assessor: Identifies the downside of each candidate move, including the worst-case replies from Black, opponent counterplay, and variance. Argues against moves that are speculative or overly complicated

Identifies the downside of each candidate move, including weakened squares, exposed kings, and lines where Stockfish gains a decisive advantage. Favors moves that keep the game balanced and avoid catastrophic mistakes
Identifies the worst-case replies from Stockfish for each candidate move, estimates the downside of aggressive options, and flags moves that rely on optimistic assumptions about the opponent's play
Identifies worst-case outcomes for each candidate move, checks for material and king-safety downside, and vetoes moves whose downside outweighs their upside. Guards against overextension
Risk Auditor: Challenges every proposed move by identifying worst-case replies, unsound sacrifices, and blunder risks such as illegal moves, hanging pieces, or repetition traps. Acts as the devil's advocate and can veto moves that fail basic safety checks
Safety Auditor: Acts as a devil's advocate by examining every candidate move for Black's best replies, including sacrifices, discovered attacks, and hidden threats against the king or loose pieces. Can veto moves that lose material or allow mate
Safety Verifier: Adversarially checks each proposed move for blunders by considering every legal Black reply, especially checks, captures, and discovered attacks. Vetoes moves that allow unacceptable replies
Tactical Calculator: Scans the current position for forcing sequences, checks, captures, and threats, calculating concrete lines several moves deep. Identifies immediate tactical opportunities for White and any Black counterplay that must be prevented
